formula: count(MR where state='merged' and merged_at in [since, until])
definition: Number of merge requests merged during the reporting window.
meaning: Overall delivery throughput via merge requests.
caveats: Depends on accurate merged_at; ignores direct pushes to default branch.

formula: count(merged MR where target_branch == default_branch and merged_at in window)
definition: Number of merged MRs targeting the project's default branch in the window.
meaning: How much change is integrated via the main branch.
caveats: If default_branch differs across repos, compare with care.

formula: count(merged MR where target_branch in {'main','master'} and merged_at in window)
definition: Number of merged MRs targeting 'main' or 'master' in the window.
meaning: Fallback integration metric for common branch names.
caveats: Not meaningful for repos using other branch names.

definition: Elapsed time from MR creation to merge.
meaning: End-to-end MR cycle time (speed of delivery).
caveats: Includes waiting time; can be skewed by weekends/holidays; use median for robustness.

definition: Average MR lead time in the window.
caveats: Sensitive to outliers; median often better.

definition: Median MR lead time in the window.
caveats: Still depends on working patterns; consider business-hours adjustment if needed.

definition: Time from MR creation to first non-author, non-system comment.
meaning: Responsiveness of code review (time to first engagement).
caveats: If reviews happen via approvals only (no comments), this may be null; bots may affect if not filtered.

formula: mean(time_to_first_review_comment_hours over merged MRs with a value)
definition: Average time to first review comment in the window.
caveats: Sensitive to outliers and missing values.

formula: median(time_to_first_review_comment_hours over merged MRs with a value)
definition: Median time to first review comment in the window.
caveats: Excludes MRs with no qualifying comments.

definition: Time from MR last update to merge.
meaning: Proxy for how long it takes to land after final activity.
caveats: updated_at changes for labels, comments, rebases; interpret cautiously.

formula: count(notes where system=false and note.author != MR.author)
definition: Number of non-system comments written by reviewers (non-author).
caveats: Some teams review via approvals or offline; counts can be low even with good review.

formula: count(distinct note.author where system=false and note.author != MR.author)
definition: Number of distinct reviewers who commented on the MR.
meaning: Breadth of participation and shared ownership.
caveats: Does not include silent reviewers; bots should be excluded if present.

definition: Average reviewer comment count per merged MR.
caveats: Can be skewed by a few large MRs.

definition: Average number of distinct commenting reviewers per MR.
caveats: Silence/approvals-only reviews reduce this.

definition: Total lines changed in the MR (adds + deletes).
meaning: MR size; larger changes generally increase risk and review time.
caveats: Not always available depending on GitLab version/permissions.

definition: Review comment density normalized by MR size.
meaning: More comparable review engagement across small vs large MRs.
caveats: If changed_lines missing or zero, metric is null.

formula: mean(comments_per_100_changed_lines over merged MRs with changed_lines>0)
definition: Average size-normalized review comment density.
meaning: Typical review engagement adjusted for change size.
caveats: Sensitive to missing changed_lines.

definition: Number of approvals required by MR approval rules at query time.
caveats: Depends on edition/config; can vary with rules and approvals reset behavior.

definition: Number of additional approvals needed at query time.
caveats: Often 0 for merged MRs; may be null if endpoint unavailable.

definition: Number of recorded approvers at query time.
caveats: Approvals can be bypassed; treat as 'what GitLab recorded'.

definition: Lines added by the MR.
caveats: May be missing in some environments.

definition: Lines deleted by the MR.
caveats: May be missing in some environments.

formula: changes_count from MR object (interpretation may vary)
definition: GitLab-reported change count (often number of changed files, depending on version).
caveats: Field semantics can vary by GitLab version; verify in your instance.

definition: Number of commits included in the MR.
meaning: Proxy for how changes are structured (many commits vs squashed).
caveats: May be null if not exposed.

formula: count(pipelines where ref==default_branch and created_at in window)
definition: Number of pipelines created on the default branch in the window.
meaning: CI usage intensity on main integration branch.
caveats: Does not include pipelines on feature branches unless you add them.

definition: Fraction of default-branch pipelines that succeeded.
caveats: Canceled pipelines counted as non-success in this implementation (failed bucket).

formula: mean(pipeline.duration over pipelines in window with a duration)
definition: Average pipeline duration on default branch.
caveats: Duration can be null for running pipelines or missing data.

formula: median(pipeline.duration over pipelines in window with a duration)
definition: Median pipeline duration on default branch.
caveats: Excludes pipelines without a duration.

formula: mean(pipeline.coverage over pipelines in window with coverage)
definition: Average code coverage as reported by GitLab pipelines (if configured).
caveats: Only valid if coverage extraction is configured consistently across repos.

formula: median(pipeline.coverage over pipelines in window with coverage)
definition: Median code coverage as reported by GitLab pipelines (if configured).
caveats: Only valid if coverage extraction is configured; otherwise null.

definition: Whether the project has a GitLab CI configuration file.
caveats: Some orgs centralize CI; this would show false.

formula: exists('README.md' or 'README.rst' or 'README.txt' on default branch)
definition: Whether the project has a README at repo root.
caveats: Docs may exist elsewhere (e.g., wiki) and not be captured.

definition: Whether a 'src' directory exists at the repo root.
caveats: Some repos use flat layout; false doesn't always imply low quality.

formula: exists('tests/' or 'test/' directory at repo root)
definition: Whether a tests directory exists at the repo root.
caveats: Tests may exist elsewhere (e.g., under package dir).

definition: Whether a docs directory exists at the repo root.
caveats: Docs may be in README only or external sites.

definition: Whether pyproject.toml is present.
meaning: Modern Python packaging/tool configuration likely used.
caveats: Some repos still use setup.cfg/setup.py; may be fine.

definition: Whether requirements files are present.
caveats: Poetry/uv/pip-tools may not use requirements.txt.

definition: Whether pre-commit configuration exists.
caveats: May be managed centrally or via CI only.

formula: exists('ruff.toml' or '.ruff.toml' or '.flake8' on default branch)
definition: Whether a linter configuration exists.
caveats: Config could be in pyproject.toml; this check misses that unless extended.

definition: Whether type checking configuration exists.
caveats: Config could be in pyproject.toml; this check misses that unless extended.

definition: Whether a Makefile exists.
caveats: Some repos use task runners (tox/nox/poe) instead.

definition: Whether a Dockerfile exists.
caveats: Deployment may not require Dockerfile (e.g., serverless).

formula: sum([has_ci, has_readme, has_src, has_tests, has_docs, (has_pyproject OR has_requirements), has_precommit, has_linter, has_typecheck, has_makefile, has_dockerfile])
definition: Aggregate score from selected repo hygiene checks.
meaning: Quick maturity score for repo foundations.
caveats: Heuristic; should be calibrated to your team standards.

formula: count(files ending with .ipynb in repo tree) when recursive scan enabled
definition: Number of Jupyter notebooks found by recursive repository tree scan (capped).
meaning: Notebook footprint (prototype vs production balance indicator).
caveats: Requires recursive scan; count may be capped by max_tree.

formula: count(files ending with .py in repo tree) when recursive scan enabled
definition: Number of Python files found by recursive repository tree scan (capped).
caveats: Requires recursive scan; count may be capped by max_tree.
